reconcile.connective: The harmonizers' strongest move is textual: the date is a copyist's slip, the original "16" miscopied as "36."

discrepancy.connective: Otto Thenius pressed the harder objection — that the Chronicler reworked and misrepresented his Kings source, so the thirty-sixth-year date reflects a real defect in Chronicles, not a recoverable scribal accident.

skeptic.name: Otto Thenius
skeptic.work: Die Bücher der Könige (Kurzgefasstes exegetisches Handbuch)
skeptic.attribution: Otto Thenius (d. 1876), Die Bücher der Könige (1849)

excerpts.excerpt_text: There remains therefore no alternative but to regard the text as erroneous - the letters ל (30) and י (10), which are somewhat similar in the ancient Hebrew characters, having been interchanged by a copyist; and hence the numbers 35 and 36 have arisen out of the original 15 and 16.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly states the harmonization for the 26-vs-36 conflict: the date is a scribal interchange of Hebrew numeral letters, original 16 became 36, removing the ten-year gap. Block-anchored; sentence drawn from deep in the KD block.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament (1861-75), on 2 Chronicles 16:1
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: K&D treat this passage directly, arguing the thirty-sixth-year date is a copyist's interchange of the Hebrew numeral letters (original 16, not 36) and that all the Chronicle's Asa data then harmonize with Kings.
